The result $14x^3 + 11x^2$ adds the absolute values $4 + 7 = 11$ for the $x^2$ terms instead of using their signs.

Since $(-11)(-12) = 132$ and $-11 + (-12) = -23$, the numerator factors as $(x - 11)(x - 12)$. Dividing by $(x - 11)$ gives $x - 12$, so $k = -12$. A common error is to use the wrong sign when identifying the factors, arriving at $k = 12$ instead of $k = -12$. Another error is to stop after identifying $11$ as a root of the denominator and conclude $k = -11$, which confuses the divisor with the quotient remainder.
